doc.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

chapter: Personal life and the future of jazz
title: Leaving for India and England
summary: Financial pressure and his marriage led Moore to India and then England, where he rediscovered music as a 'born again musician'.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I hope they have some for you tonight. What, if you don’t mind me asking, caused you to want to leave the country?

Oh it was a lot of personal reasons, but financial pressure to a great extent. My wife at the time was of Indian origin. And I was living in Pennsylvania, I was driving 150 miles back and forth every day to work a lot of the time, and barely making ends meet, and things weren’t so good financially. And we had the idea of kind of selling our house and moving to India. My son could have gone to private school there with the money we got from selling our house — they were giving 13% tax free interest on it. Over there we could have lived very well. I had this thing I was going to start writing and have my son go to private school. He was young at the time, five or six. And then we’d come back and play, and basically walk away from the rat race. But it didn’t work out. Inflation was running at 18%, and so on the fixed income, that was going to be going down. My son would have never caught up in school. They start them at like the age of two over there, or three years old. So there was whole lot of other reasons. So Plan B was to go to England. And it was actually a very good learning experience for me, a growth experience. Because first of all I had gotten to the point where I almost didn’t enjoy going to work anymore, didn’t enjoy playing music, didn’t enjoy the life anymore, and I wanted it to be over. And when I got to England and subsequently that marriage broke up, and all of a sudden I was back in music. I had students and I was playing piano and I went out and I re-discovered that I had this whole life in music, and I re-discovered the love of playing and it was like, people talk about being born again Christians, I was a born again musician. And I started with a whole new attitude. And it was a very good growth experience. It was, you know they say when things are at their absolute worst, wait, and it could be the best thing to
happen. And it turned out the whole process was a very good reaffirmation of music and life.
